data.name: Jabreel
data.gender_notes: Jabreel is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Jabreel is an Arabic name derived from the word Jabar, meaning 'to be generous or glorify'. In Islamic tradition, Jabreel is the name of the Angel of Death and the Angel of Revelation. The name Jabreel carries the meaning “Glorifier of God” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Jabreel usually hope their child will grow to embody glorifier of god and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes dedication and devotion to God.
data.etymology: Jabreel belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Glorifier of God.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Jabreel total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

in_english.name: Jabreel
in_english.meaning: One of the chief angels in Islam
in_english.long_meaning: Jabreel, also known as Gabriel, is one of the chief angels in Islam. He is considered the angel of revelation, tasked with communicating God's messages to prophets, particularly the Prophet Muhammad. The name originates from the Arabic root 'j-b-r' meaning 'to prevail' or 'to be powerful'

data.cultural_impact: Jabreel is considered a significant name in Islamic culture, as it is associated with two major figures in Islamic belief - the Angel of Death and the Angel of Revelation. The Angel of Death is believed to take the soul at the time of death, while the Angel of Revelation is responsible for delivering divine messages to Prophets and other important figures. The name carries the weight and importance of these roles, making it a respected and revered name in Islamic communities.
data.spiritual_significance: Jabreel is believed to hold great spiritual significance in Islam, as it is associated with two key aspects of the human experience - death and divine revelation. The name Jabreel is a reminder of the cyclical nature of life, where birth, growth, decay, and death are all part of the natural order. Additionally, the name is a reminder of the connection between the physical world and the divine realm, as angels like Jabreel serve as messengers and conveyors of God's will to humanity. The name Jabreel is therefore a reminder of the sacred bond between the Creator and the created, and the importance of staying spiritually connected to God throughout one's life.
